steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Command words tell you exactly what the examiner expects: 'describe' means give an account, 'explain' means give reasons, 'analyse' means break down and examine, 'evaluate' means make a judgement.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Describe questions require you to identify and outline film language features or production contexts without needing to explain their effect.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Explain questions require you to give reasons why something produces a particular effect or meaning, connecting technique to impact.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Analyse questions require you to break down a sequence or concept into its component parts and examine how they work together to create meaning.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always identify the command word first and plan your response around exactly what it asks you to do. For 'evaluate' questions, make sure you reach a clear judgement and do not just analyse without concluding. Use precise film language terminology throughout: examiner mark schemes reward correct technical vocabulary. In extended answers, structure your response with a clear introduction, focused paragraphs and a conclusion that answers the question. Check that every paragraph actually addresses the question set, not just the general topic area.
